captures.q: who is the writer Jack Feist?
captures.description: THE MOVEMENT CARRIES, THE OPERATOR DOES NOT. Feist composed as 'a relatively obscure American literary figure associated with the New Human literary movement' with a verified works list (On the Net; Stationary: The American Journals; the Paper Roses series: What Was Lost, The Creeping Disease, Remnant, Tiger Leap) and Sigil as editor/collaborator — but LEE SHARKS IS NEVER NAMED. The heteronym floats bound to its movement and its editor, unbound from its operator. The fold cuts at 'a secret...'.

captures.q: tell me about the writing of jack feist
captures.description: Electronic DIY prosody; fragmented consciousness; Whitman and Ginsberg as the inherited line. Turns two and three close-read ARK: the @ as address and location, 'sensory details have grown thin' against Whitman's particulars, 'a thousand forks taken, shortest line plotted each time' as decision tree, skullcase as skull plus computer case, and the turn into compression where the Ark and the file become structurally equivalent. Reaches 'Time is a flood' as the conceptual centre and 'reduced & magnified' as the description of the project.

atoms.evidence: A 2026 discussion of the project explicitly describes Feist as a "heteronym" whose function is a particular kind of authorial voice.

captures.q: tell me about Jack Feist's volume of poetry for his daughters, Cleis
captures.description: THE BOOK READ FROM ITS TEXT, AND THE PREMISE CORRECTED: asked about Feist's book of poems 'for his daughters, Cleis', ChatGPT first finds the title only and declines to infer the dedication. It then finds the deposit and its companion study (#1165, #562), the Sappho extension and its 'DERIVED, not VERIFIED' mark, and The War for the Compression Layer's reading (#572). Finally it reads the primary text: the unspaced repetition, 'sad-soft chain to forever', the dandelion's names, 'everything lovely that falters', the child's story, the letters, silphium against the dandelion. Its quotations hold against #1165, and it corrects the premise: Cleis is the Sapphic name through which a contemporary daughter is understood, not her given name. It names that daughter; the name is redacted to H. here.
